title: Early Planet Formation in Embedded Disks (eDisk). XIII. Aligned Disks with Nonsettled Dust around the Newly Resolved Class 0 Protobinary R CrA IRAS 32
question: Characterize the newly resolved Class 0 protobinary IRAS 32 (disk sizes, dust masses, alignment, dust settling, outflows, gas kinematics) and what these imply for how the binary formed

data.angular_resolution: ~0.03 arcsec (~5 au) continuum; ~0.1 arcsec for molecular lines; continuum beam 35 x 23 mas
data.sensitivity: continuum RMS 0.02 mJy/beam (0.026 in table note); line-cube RMS values in line results table

what.value: Distance of 150 pc, taken as a convenient value consistent with Gaia parallaxes

evidence.quote: The distance is taken to be 150 pc as a convenient value that is in agreement with recent Gaia parallax estimations

what.value: Dust mass opacity kappa = 2.3 cm2 g-1 at 225 GHz

evidence.quote: We adopt a dust mass opacity, $\kappa_{\nu}$ = 2.3 cm$^{2}$ g$^{-1}$ at $\nu=225$ GHz (cite: beckwith1990).

what.value: Dust temperature prescription T_dust = T0 (L_bol/1 Lsun)^0.25 with T0 = 43 K

evidence.quote: given the bolometric luminosity prescription from (cite: tobin2020)

what.value: Bolometric luminosity L_bol = 1.6 Lsun from an SED fit

evidence.quote: IRAS 32 has L$_{bol}$ = 1.6 L$_{\odot}$ via a spectral energy distribution (SED) fit compiled from the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) database (cite: edisk)

what.value: Bolometric temperature of 64 K, implying a Class 0 classification

evidence.quote: a more careful fit to the photometry of the source gives a bolometric temperature of 64 K, which suggests that IRAS 32 is better described as a Class 0 source (cite: edisk)

recipe.goal: Combine execution blocks and self-calibrate the continuum
recipe.method: Combine all six EBs, rescale fluxes to the 2021-08-18 EB, run four phase-only self-cal iterations (inf-EB, inf, 18.14 s, int) then amplitude+phase self-cal at inf; self-cal also tested on short baselines alone and compared
key_parameters: Phase-only solution intervals: inf-EB, inf, 18.14 sec, int; then amplitude and phase at inf

recipe.method: Briggs weighting, robust -0.5, mtmfs deconvolver, primary-beam corrected, on combined data; low-resolution map from short-baseline data only

recipe.goal: Fit Gaussians to the continuum to get flux density, sizes and PA
recipe.method: Simultaneous two-Gaussian fit to the high-resolution map (one per disk); simultaneous three-Gaussian fit to the low-resolution map (two disks plus circumbinary structure)
key_parameters: Gaussian fit peak intensity not used in the analysis because it is less robust than total flux
Circumbinary-structure quantities have errors of order ~10%; main purpose was the PA

recipe.goal: Derive inclination, disk radius and dust mass
recipe.method: Inclination from arccos(b/a) of the fitted Gaussian; radius as 2-sigma value of deconvolved major axis; dust mass from optically thin isothermal Equation with T = 20 K and T = 40.7 K
key_parameters: d = 150 pc; kappa = 2.3 cm2 g-1 at 225 GHz; T0 = 43 K; L_bol = 1.6 Lsun split 50% each giving T_dust = 40.7 K
assumptions: Dust mass opacity 2.3 cm2 g-1 at 225 GHz (Beckwith et al. 1990)
Isothermal, optically thin emission; masses are lower limits since disks likely not optically thin
Temperature of 20 K as the first case

recipe.goal: Check continuum radial profiles and near/far-side asymmetry
recipe.method: Intensity profiles along the major and minor axes of each source; near/far side assigned using the CO outflow; brightness asymmetry along minor axis interpreted as optically thick, geometrically thick, unsettled dust

recipe.goal: Make line cubes and moment maps
recipe.method: Continuum-subtracted cubes imaged like the continuum but with auto-multithresh masks and briggsbwtaper, robust 0.5; moment 0 and 1 with bettermoments using >3 sigma cuts; adopted systemic velocity 5.86 km/s
key_parameters: Moment maps clipped at 3 sigma; auto-multithresh default parameters
assumptions: Systemic velocity 5.86 km/s adopted by visual inspection of the cube and used for all molecules

recipe.goal: Fit rotation curves in PV diagrams and derive enclosed masses
recipe.method: PV diagrams made with CASA impv; SLAM pvanalysis fits ridge and edge of the 13CO PV diagrams with a power law v = V_b (r/R_b)^-p; mass from M = V_b^2 R_b / (G sin^2 i); central velocity left free
key_parameters: PV cut angle = Gaussian-fit position angles; PV line width ~1 beam
Source A PV extended to 2 arcsec, source B to 1.5 arcsec; only the opposite side of each disk fitted to limit contamination
assumptions: p ~ 0.5 consistent with Keplerian rotation; p ~ 1 with rotation plus infall conserving angular momentum; ridge and edge fits bracket the Keplerian mass; inclination from the continuum fits

recipe.method: Deprojected dynamical age from deprojected maximum 12CO outflow velocity and projected outflow length
key_parameters: Projected length ~20 arcsec (3000 au); maximum velocity ~17 km/s from visual inspection of the cube; inclination 70 deg
assumptions: Inclination of 70 deg is the average of the disk inclination fits

score_reason: Project code, CASA version, self-cal intervals, robust values, deconvolver, formulae, kappa, temperature prescription and numeric tables are given, but calibration details, imaging sizes/thresholds, line-free channels and SLAM configuration are deferred to the eDisk overview paper or omitted.
rediscovery_reason: Data are from a Large Program stated to be going into the public archive, the continuum recipe (self-cal intervals, robust -0.5, mtmfs, Gaussian fits, dust-mass formula) is mostly specified, and main results (radii, masses, SLAM fits) are numeric; gaps in imaging parameters mean values will match only approximately.
